blocks.task_summary: Find α and β for which the linear system has infinitely many solutions.
method_path: Set third row coefficients to zero for consistency
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Eliminate one variable, substitute into third equation, set coefficients to zero.
METHOD 3: Add/subtract equations, compare coefficients with third equation.
METHOD 4: Vector approach: find direction vector of intersection of first two planes, require normal of third plane perpendicular to it, then find β using a common point.
METHOD 5: Find general point on line of intersection of first two planes, substitute into third plane, require coefficient of parameter zero and constant term equal to β.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1 Row Reduction: attempt to reduce a matrix or eliminate one variable (M1); two correct rows or equivalent equations A1A1; correct third row or equivalent equation A1; equating the third row coefficients to zero (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.

METHOD 2 Writing an equation in one variable: attempt to eliminate either x or z using the first two equations (M1); one correct equation A1; correct substitution into the third equation to create an equation in either x or z A2; attempt to set coefficients equal to zero for infinite solutions (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.
METHOD 3 Subtracting and comparing equations: attempt to add or subtract two equations (M1); A2; attempt to compare coefficients with the third equation (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1A1.

METHOD 4 Vector approach: attempt to find direction vector of line of intersection using π1 and π2 (M1); d = (2, -3, 2) A1; normal of π3 is perpendicular to d (M1); α = 2 A1; correct substitution of a point common to the first two planes into the third plane A1; β = 10 A1.

METHOD 5 Finding a general point on the line of intersection: attempt to find intersection of π1 and π2 (M1); x = 4 + 2t, y = 3 - 3t, z = 2t A1A1; correct substitution of general point into π3 A1; recognizing that the coefficient of t must be zero OR the constant term must be β (M1); α = 2 and β = 10 A1.
